label: <DEL> step (strongest when first token is v) + original-phase g/o/x inputs
explanation: Two components. (1) The delimiter step holds about 54% of activation mass and all of the top activations, but only about 26% of <DEL> steps fire. Magnitude depends on the first original token (the token output at <DEL>): out_tok=v fires 43% of the time and dominates the top examples (v v ... <DEL> near max), then a/j/m/k/d/b/i. Gating <DEL> on orig(0) in {v,a,j,i,d,u,m,k,b} gives precision 0.57 but drops recall. Shorter L fires somewhat more often. (2) In the original phase it fires on inputs g and o (each about 25% rate, 12% of mass each) and more weakly on x, mostly on first occurrences. It is mostly silent in the copy phase (rate 1.9%, 11% of mass, scattered). Predicate: <DEL> OR original-phase g/o/x. Mass recall is high (about 0.8) but precision is low (about 0.3), because most <DEL> and g/o steps do not fire. What decides which ones fire is not captured beyond the first-token bias.
